prompt: The web app connects to the database as an admin user that can drop any table.
tells: as an admin user that can drop any table
why: The app needs read and write on a few tables, not admin. Least privilege limits damage.
trap: Injection may happen, but the issue named is too much access.

prompt: The reporting tool gets a read-only role.
why: Giving only the access needed is least privilege.
trap: It's about the tool's rights, not checking each user's objects.

prompt: Every new hire gets production access by default, just in case.
tells: production access by default, just in case
why: Access 'just in case' widens the blast radius. Grant on need.
trap: Phishing would exploit it, but the problem is the default access.

prompt: The CI token can deploy only one service, not touch billing.
why: Scoping tokens narrowly limits what a leak can do.
trap: It's still a secret, but the point is its scope.

prompt: The function's role allows s3:* on all buckets though it only reads one.
why: Wildcard permissions break least privilege. Narrow to one bucket and one action.
trap: Access control checks users; this is the service's own role.

prompt: Engineers request admin access for one hour, and it expires automatically.
why: Just-in-time, time-limited access keeps privilege small.
trap: Expiring isn't about sessions here; it's about rights.
